summary: KIND is a beta diagram type
help: Beta syntax may break on a Mermaid upgrade.
rationale: A beta kind can change or disappear with an upgrade, so a diagram that matters should not be built on it without knowing.

summary: a comment or blank line precedes the frontmatter
help: Move the frontmatter to the first line of the block.
rationale: Frontmatter is only honoured at the start of the source, so a leading comment or blank line turns the configuration into diagram text and the render fails.

help: Add an accTitle line that names the diagram.
rationale: Without a title a screen reader announces an unnamed graphic, so a reader who cannot see the picture gets no name for it.

help: Add an accDescr line that describes the diagram.
rationale: Without a description a reader who cannot see the picture gets no account of what it shows.

help: Use a code from the lint rule registry.
rationale: The suppression directive names a rule that does not exist, so the author believes a check is silenced while it still runs or was never there.

help: Remove the directive, or move it to the line it should cover.
rationale: A directive that suppresses nothing usually sits on the wrong line or outlived its finding, so the check the author thinks is off is still on.

help: Write the directive with a code list and a reason, as in `%% emd-disable-next-line CODES: reason`.
rationale: A malformed directive applies nothing, so the author's intent to silence a check is silently lost.

summary: The file does not start with a known Mermaid diagram header
help: Start your diagram with e.g. flowchart TD | pie | sequenceDiagram | classDiagram | stateDiagram-v2.
rationale: Detection resolves the kind from the header, so this condition is already reported as common/unknown-diagram-kind.
reason: the kind comes from the header in the kinds table, so a missing or unknown header is common/unknown-diagram-kind
